A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PhishBencher work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on contamination detection, model-progress tracking, cross-language contamination, pretraining, and model merging in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds experiments on answer recovery, reasoning, prompt sensitivity, and additional model configurations.

M1.justification: Section 3 adds an explicit sample-based estimator that converts phished answer matches into an estimate of original accuracy. This is a limited scoring extension; the benchmark randomization procedure and binomial contamination detector are retained.

E1.justification: V2 adds an adversarial answer-recovery scenario across eight benchmarks, supplying models with randomized answers and transformation rules (Table 3). It also includes MMLU-Pro and GPQA-diamond in the expanded evaluations. The recovery task substantially extends the tested requirements, while the existing QA domains and six-language coverage remain.

E2.justification: The competing contamination detector remains the BIG-bench canary-string approach, evaluated through log probabilities and GUID completion. Additional LLMs are evaluation subjects, and the new reasoning and unphished conditions are controls. The revised canary sampling procedure changes evaluation settings rather than comparator membership.

E3.justification: GUID completion changes from one temperature-zero completion per prefix to 1,000 queries at each of 11 temperatures, counting any successful completion (v1 Appendix B.2; v2 B.3). Model-progress tracking changes from full benchmark sizes to samples of at most 1,024 and expands from three Llama models to eleven models. V2 also adds 14B configurations, correlation metrics, and protocols for the new controlled analyses.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained Bayes-accuracy sensitivity and cross-language experiments, v2 adds reverse-engineering attacks, reasoning versus no-reasoning analysis, nine prompt variants, training on original versus phished data, and checks for ignored randomization instructions (Table 3, Appendix B.2, and Figures 16–18). These test previously unexamined robustness and mechanism questions.

E5.justification: V2 adds Kendall rank-correlation estimates and associated p-values for individual benchmarks and aggregate performance (Table 6). Both versions retain the stated three-seed mean/standard-deviation convention and the 5% binomial detection test; no increase in independent experimental runs is stated.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial ranking, scaling, recovery, and diagnostic results. Table 6 reports aggregate Kendall's tau of 0.96, but GPQA has tau 0.35 and p=0.16; new Table 3 reports GPQA recovery accuracy of 47.87% versus 37.82% with original prompts. GUID-completion curves are replaced under the expanded sampling protocol. The pretraining and model-merging values in Tables 1–2 are unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 derives an unbiased original-accuracy estimator, adds Theorem 2 giving its variance and mean squared error, and supplies its proof in Appendix A.2. Theorem 1, Corollary 1, and their proofs are retained. The algebraic description of Z/KZ is also corrected from a finite field to an additive group.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central claims: randomized benchmarks permit evaluation without fully disclosing true answers and enable contamination detection through a Bayes-accuracy ceiling. The conclusion additionally mentions theoretical support, without redefining the principal contribution.

C2.justification: V2 explains the estimator's precision cost, difficulties distinguishing small performance gaps, why benchmark-generated randomness suffices, and reasoning's role in instruction compliance. It newly qualifies disclosure-allowed defenses as addressing benign leakage and acknowledges stronger answer-recovery attacks. It also revises the canary-completion interpretation and softens eliminating a second private test set to potentially reducing that need.

D1.justification: V2 adds explicit reverse-engineering and prompt-variation templates (Tables 7–8), detailed canary query and temperature settings, H100 hardware information for 14B models, and MMLU-Pro access information. Existing dataset-access and model-merging implementation references are retained; these are bounded additions to reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning against memorization audits, membership inference, and dynamic evaluation. New discussions distinguish dataset-level detection from example-level membership inference and answer randomization from question regeneration, citing work such as Carlini and Panda's canary research, VarBench, DyVal, DARG, and KIEval.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much existing prose are retained. V2 locally rewrites methods and results passages, presents practical strategies as bullets, and adds appendix subheadings. The private-evaluation rewrite also introduces an unfinished 'underlying xxx' placeholder.

P2.justification: The model-progress bar charts become scatterplots with model and release-date encodings. V2 adds reasoning, robustness, and control plots plus recovery, correlation, and prompt tables, and expands or rearranges model panels. The existing dataset-size table is expanded and renumbered from Table 3 to Table 5, rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: Theorem 2 and its proof quantify a previously unexamined precision cost, while the expanded ranking study replaces a three-Llama demonstration with broader quantitative evidence. New controlled analyses probe instruction-following and concealment failures, addressing central validation gaps in v1. Attack-resilience conclusions remain limited by the simple attacks tested, and an unfinished private-evaluation passage reduces polish, but these weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial gains in analytical and empirical scrutiny.
